units.source_text: 且说右近将谢绝匂亲王访问之事告诉了浮舟。

en.t: Ukone told Ukifune that she had refused Prince Niou's visit.

units.source_text: 浮舟闻之，心绪更加混乱了，一直躺在那里。

en.t: When Ukifune heard this, her thoughts grew even more confused, and she lay there without rising.

units.source_text: 正在此时，侍从回来，把情况一一告知了浮舟。

en.t: Just then, the attendant returned and told Ukifune everything that had happened.

units.source_text: 浮舟一言不答，然而眼泪几乎使枕头浮了起来。

en.t: Ukifune did not answer a word, but her tears nearly made the pillow float.

units.source_text: 又恐侍女们看见了诧怪，只得努力隐忍。

en.t: Afraid that the serving women would notice and wonder, she could only struggle to hold herself back.

units.source_text: 次日早晨，自知两眼红肿难于见人，一直躺着不肯起身。

en.t: The next morning, knowing that her red, swollen eyes made her unfit to face anyone, she kept lying down and would not get up.

units.source_text: 后来勉强披衣束带，起来诵经。

en.t: Later, she forced herself to put on her clothes and sash, got up, and chanted sutras.

units.source_text: 她一心指望消减先亲而死的罪孽。

en.t: She single-mindedly hoped to lessen the sin of dying before her parents.

units.source_text: 又取出那天匂亲王所绘的画来看看，觉得他描绘时的姿态和俊俏的面貌，历历如在目前。

en.t: She also took out the picture Prince Niou had drawn that day and looked at it, feeling that his posture as he painted and his handsome face stood vividly before her eyes.

units.source_text: 想起昨夜不能和他交谈一语，今天倍觉悲痛，无限伤心。

en.t: Remembering that she had not been able to exchange even a single word with him the night before, she felt twice as sorrowful today and was endlessly heartbroken.

units.source_text: 又想起那薰大将：“他指望迎我入京，从容相见，永远聚首。

en.t: Then she thought of General Kaoru: "He hoped to bring me to the capital, meet me at ease, and remain with me forever.

units.source_text: 一旦听到了我的死耗，不知作何感想，实在对他不起。

en.t: If he hears the news of my death, I do not know what he will feel; I have truly wronged him.

units.source_text: 我死之后，世间恐怕也有非难我的人，想起了深觉可耻。

en.t: After I die, there will probably be people in the world who blame me, and when I think of that, I feel deeply ashamed.

units.source_text: 然而与其活在世间，被人指为浮薄女子，当作笑柄，恶评传入薰大将耳中，则远不如死。

en.t: Yet rather than live on in the world, be pointed at as a frivolous woman, become a laughingstock, and have such slander reach General Kaoru's ears, it would be far better to die.
